rules.title: Every game piece has an owner.

rules.title: You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.).
rules.text: 1.7.1. You “own” the pieces you bring to the game (your deck, side deck, Gig dice, etc.). You’re the “owner” of these pieces.

rules.text: 1.7.2. You “control” the pieces currently in your friendly Gig area, field, Legends area, and Eddies area. You’re the “controller” of these pieces, even if you’re not the owner.

rules.text: 1.7.2.1. Pieces you control are considered “friendly” pieces.

rules.title: Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners.
rules.text: 1.7.3. Game pieces can change controllers, but can never change owners.

rules.title: At the end of the game, return all game pieces to their respective owners.

rules.title: Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.
rules.text: 2.3. Resolve card effects in the order they appear on the card.

rules.title: If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.
rules.text: 2.4. If you can’t resolve the entirety of an effect, resolve as much of it as you possibly can.

rules.title: If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.
rules.text:
2.5. If a card’s text contradicts the Official Rules, the card text supersedes the Official Rules.

> **EXAMPLE:** According to the rules, you can’t attack a ready Unit, but a friendly Unit’s card text reads “This Unit can attack ready Units.” The card text overrides that rule, so the friendly Unit can declare an attack on a rival ready Unit.

rules.title: A game value can be a negative number.
rules.text: 2.10. A game value can be a negative number.

rules.title: When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.
rules.text:
2.10.1. When a game value is a negative number, it is treated as 0 for all references and comparisons of values.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit has 2 power. An effect reduces its power by 3. The Unit has -1 power, but is treated as having 0 power when attacking, fighting, or when a card effect references its power. If it then gains +2 power, that Unit has 1 power. The order of these effects being applied does not alter this outcome.

rules.title: A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number.
rules.text: 2.10.2. A value of null ( - ) is not treated as a number. It does not count as 0, and it is not even or odd.

rules.text: 3.4.1. While a card is face-down, ignore all card information, except whether or not the card is a Legend. (As indicated by the cardback design.)

rules.text: 3.17.3.1. Units and Legends inherit power from Gears equipped to them.

rules.text: 3.17.3.2. A Gear’s power is equal to the power printed on the card.

rules.text: 3.17.3.3. A Gear’s power is not modified by card effects, unless the effect specifically targets the Gear.

rules.text: 3.17.4. “Base power” refers to the printed power on a Legend, Unit, or Gear, separate from any applied or inherited modifiers.

rules.title: Textbox
rules.text: 3.18. ### Textbox

rules.title: A card’s textbox contains its card text.
rules.text: 3.18.1. A card’s textbox contains its card text.

rules.title: A card may have multiple textboxes.
rules.text: 3.18.1.1. A card may have multiple textboxes.

rules.title: “Card text” may include effect text, reminder text, and flavor text, differentiated by formatting and treatment.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2. “Card text” may include effect text, reminder text, and flavor text, differentiated by formatting and treatment.

rules.title: “Effect text” is any text on a card that dictates a game effect.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.1. “Effect text” is any text on a card that dictates a game effect.

rules.title: Effect text may use symbols or keywords as shorthand for longer effects, conditions, or concepts.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.1.1. Effect text may use symbols or keywords as shorthand for longer effects, conditions, or concepts. See TERMS.

rules.title: “Reminder text” reminds you of relevant rules, keyword definitions, or other implied effects.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.2. “Reminder text” reminds you of relevant rules, keyword definitions, or other implied effects.

rules.title: Reminder text is not effect text, and does not influence gameplay.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.2.1. Reminder text is not effect text, and does not influence gameplay.

rules.title: Reminder text is always italicized and parenthetical.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.2.2. Reminder text is always italicized and parenthetical.

rules.title: “Flavor text” is non-gameplay text that adds lore to a card.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.3. “Flavor text” is non-gameplay text that adds lore to a card.

rules.title: Flavor text is always italicized.
rules.text: 3.18.1.2.3.1. Flavor text is always italicized.

rules.title: Card text addresses the player who played the card.
rules.text: 3.18.2. Card text addresses the player who played the card. When an effect says “you,” it’s referring to the player controlling the card.

rules.title: While a Gear is equipped to a Unit or Legend, that Unit or Legend inherits any text in the Gear’s bottom textbox.
rules.text: 3.18.3. While a Gear is equipped to a Unit or Legend, that Unit or Legend inherits any text in the Gear’s bottom textbox. See CARD TYPES > Gears.

rules.title: RAM Limits
rules.text:
3.20.3. #### RAM Limits

A deck’s 3 Legends provide your deck’s “RAM Limits.” All other cards in your deck must be within these RAM Limits.

rules.title: By default, decks have a RAM Limit of 0 in all colors (0 Red, 0 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).
rules.text: 3.20.4. By default, decks have a RAM Limit of 0 in all colors (0 Red, 0 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).

rules.title: When you add a Legend to your deck, increase the deck’s RAM Limits by the Legend’s RAM value.
rules.text: 3.20.5. When you add a Legend to your deck, increase the deck’s RAM Limits by the Legend’s RAM value.

rules.title: A deck’s RAM Limit in a color is the sum of its Legends’ RAM in that color.
rules.text:
3.20.5.1. A deck’s RAM Limit in a color is the sum of its Legends’ RAM in that color.

> **EXAMPLE:** A deck with “Goro Takemura: Hands Unclean” (2 Green RAM), “Saburo Arasaka: Stubborn Patriarch” (2 Green RAM), and “Yorinobu Arasaka: Embracing Destruction” (2 Red RAM), has a RAM Limit of (2 Red, 4 Green, 0 Blue, and 0 Yellow).

rules.title: Your deck may include any card with RAM less than or equal to your deck’s RAM Limit for its color.
rules.text: 3.20.5.2. Your deck may include any card with RAM less than or equal to your deck’s RAM Limit for its color.

rules.title: Your deck’s RAM Limits are locked after deck composition.
rules.text: 3.20.6. Your deck’s RAM Limits are locked after deck composition. If a Legend is removed from the game during play, your deck’s RAM Limits are not affected.

rules.title: RAM values do not dictate ability to play a card, simply whether it’s legal to include in your deck.
rules.text: 3.20.6.1. RAM values do not dictate ability to play a card, simply whether it’s legal to include in your deck.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Gear’s top text box contains the reminder text “*(Equip to a friendly Unit or face-up Legend.)*” You equip this Gear to a friendly Unit. That Gear cannot be equipped to another friendly Unit, nor face-up Legend.

rules.text: 4.11.3.2. A Unit or Legend does not inherit Tags or other characteristics from a Gear equipped to it.

rules.text: 4.12. When a Legend or Unit moves to a different area (field, trash, hand, etc.), all of its equipped Gear moves with it.

rules.title: When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to t…
rules.text:
4.12.1. When a Gear moves with a Unit or Legend to an area outside of the field or Legends area, the Gear isn’t equipped to the Unit or Legend in that area.

> **EXAMPLE:** An equipped Unit has the effect “At the end of your turn, return this Unit to its owner's hand.” When you move the Unit to your hand, you also move its equipped Gear to your hand. Once the cards are in your hand, the Gear is no longer equipped to the Unit. So, if you play the Unit from your hand next turn, the Gear does not move with it.

rules.text: 4.12.2. If an equipped Legend moves to an area outside of the Field or Legends area, the Gear follows the Legend to the new area. The Gear is no longer equipped in the new area, so it stays there when you remove the Legend from play.

rules.title: When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order.
rules.text: 4.12.3. When you bottom-deck an equipped Unit, place the cards at the bottom of your deck in a random order. Randomize them amongst any other cards bottom-decked at the same time. See Bottom-deck.

rules.title: Legends Area
rules.text: 5.7. ### Legends Area

rules.title: Each player places their three Legends face-down and randomized in this area at the start of the game.
rules.text: 5.7.1. Each player places their three Legends face-down and randomized in this area at the start of the game.

rules.title: You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down.
rules.text: 5.7.2. You can spend any number of Legends in this area as 1 €$ each, whether face-up or face-down.

rules.title: While you can spend a Legend to pay 1 €$ toward a cost, Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies.
rules.text: 5.7.2.1. While you can spend a Legend to pay 1 €$ toward a cost, Legends are not considered Eddies, and cannot become Eddies.

rules.text: 5.7.2.2. If a face-up Legend does not have a Sell Tag, you may not spend it for 1 €$.

rules.title: “Call a Legend” may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to “Call a Legend”.
rules.text: 5.7.3. “Call a Legend” may be used only once per turn even if a game action tells you to “Call a Legend”.

rules.title: The Legends area is a public area.
rules.text: 5.7.4. The Legends area is a public area. Players can count the number of cards any player has in this area and read them at any time.

rules.title: The face-down Legends in this area are hidden.
rules.text: 5.7.4.1. The face-down Legends in this area are hidden. You cannot look at them unless specified otherwise.

rules.title: If you learn the location of one or more face-down Legend(s), visually distinguish any “known” Legends to your Rival…
rules.text: 5.7.4.2. If you learn the location of one or more face-down Legend(s), visually distinguish any “known” Legends to your Rival without revealing them. This can be with a token marker, or by physically separating known Legends from unknown Legends.

rules.title: If an effect asks you to look at a face-down legend, you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unles…
rules.text: 5.7.4.3. If an effect asks you to look at a face-down legend, you cannot look at it again once that effect has resolved, unless otherwise specified.

rules.title: You may pay a Legend’s cost to play it from the Legends area to the field as a Unit.
rules.text: 5.7.5. You may pay a Legend’s cost to play it from the Legends area to the field as a Unit. See CARD TYPES > Legends.

rules.title: A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.
rules.text: 5.7.6. A Legend in the Legend area may use its [Spend Icon] at any point it is face-up in the Legend’s area.

rules.title: There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.
rules.text: 5.7.7. There is no limit of cards that can be in the Legends area.

rules.title: The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).
rules.text: 5.9.1. The trash area is also referred to as just “the trash” or “your trash” (and variations thereof).

rules.text: 5.9.4. When placing new cards in this area, they are placed on top of the previous card already in the pile.

rules.title: Fixer Area
rules.text: 5.10. ### Fixer Area

rules.title: The fixer area is where you place your dice during Pre-Game Setup {GAME SETUP > Pre-Game Setup}.
rules.text: 5.10.1. The fixer area is where you place your dice during Pre-Game Setup. Dice remain in the fixer area until you roll them in during you Main Phase.

rules.title: The fixer area is a public area.
rules.text: 5.10.2. The fixer area is a public area. Both players can freely view the Gig dice in this area.

rules.text: 5.10.4. Card effects that interact with Gigs do not apply to Gig dice in the fixer area unless the fixer area is explicitly mentioned.

rules.text: 5.10.5. While your fixer area has no dice in it, it is considered “empty.”

rules.title: GIGS
rules.text: GIGS

rules.title: 1 polyhedral die represents 1 Gig.
rules.text: 6.1. 1 polyhedral die represents 1 Gig. Gigs are also referred to as “Gig dice” (and variations thereof).

rules.title: Gig dice are represented by d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20.
rules.text: 6.1.1. Gig dice are represented by d4, d6, d8, d10, d12, d20. These designations refer both to the number of sides on a die and the highest value a die can reach.

rules.title: You control the Gigs in your Gig area.
rules.text: 6.1.2. You control the Gigs in your Gig area. They are considered “friendly Gigs”.

rules.title: You don’t control the Gig dice in your fixer area.
rules.text: 6.1.3. You don’t control the Gig dice in your fixer area. They are not considered friendly Gigs.

rules.title: You can’t target Gig dice in the fixer area to fulfill or resolve effects.
rules.text: 6.1.4. You can’t target Gig dice in the fixer area to fulfill or resolve effects.

rules.title: Whenever you roll a die, you may use any method you want as long as it is timely and meets these requirements:
rules.text: 6.2. Whenever you roll a die, you may use any method you want as long as it is timely and meets these requirements:

rules.title: Your roll method properly randomizes the die faces.
rules.text: 6.2.1. Your roll method properly randomizes the die faces.

rules.title: The result is immediately visible when the die stops rolling.
rules.text: 6.2.2. The result is immediately visible when the die stops rolling.

rules.title: No one touches the rolling die or interferes with its trajectory until it is completely still and shows a definitive…
rules.text: 6.2.3. No one touches the rolling die or interferes with its trajectory until it is completely still and shows a definitive result.

rules.title: The die lands on a definitive result, not cocked between faces.
rules.text: 6.2.4. The die lands on a definitive result, not cocked between faces.

rules.title: If your roll breaks any of the above rules, ignore the result and roll it again properly.
rules.text: 6.2.5. If your roll breaks any of the above rules, ignore the result and roll it again properly.

rules.title: When you move a die to the area of play after rolling, you must preserve the value.
rules.text: 6.2.6. When you move a die to the area of play after rolling, you must preserve the value.

rules.title: A Gig’s value is the number on its current top face.
rules.text: 6.3. A Gig’s value is the number on its current top face.

rules.title: A min Gig is any Gig die at its lowest possible value.
rules.text: 6.3.1. A min Gig is any Gig die at its lowest possible value.

rules.title: A max Gig is any Gig die at its highest possible value.
rules.text:
6.3.2. A max Gig is any Gig die at its highest possible value.

> **EXAMPLE:** A d4 has four sides with possible values of 1, 2, 3, and 4. If its current value is 4, then it’s a max Gig.

rules.title: The highest value on a die is always equal to its number of sides, and the lowest value on a die is always 1.
rules.text:
6.3.3. The highest value on a die is always equal to its number of sides, and the lowest value on a die is always 1. This is true even if the specific die represents the number differently.

> **EXAMPLE:** If the faces of your d10 are labelled 0-9, the 0 represents “10” and is considered the highest value, while the 1 is considered the lowest value.

rules.title: Adjust a Gig by changing its value.
rules.text: 6.4. Adjust a Gig by changing its value.

rules.title: “Increase” a Gig by adjusting to a higher number.
rules.text: 6.4.1. “Increase” a Gig by adjusting to a higher number.

rules.title: “Decrease” a Gig by adjusting to a lower number.
rules.text: 6.4.2. “Decrease” a Gig by adjusting to a lower number.

rules.title: “Set” a Gig by adjusting it to a specific value.
rules.text: 6.4.3. “Set” a Gig by adjusting it to a specific value.

rules.title: You cannot adjust a Gig to a value that isn’t on its face.
rules.text: 6.4.4. You cannot adjust a Gig to a value that isn’t on its face. (i.e. set a d6 to 8). If an effect tells you to do so, the effect fails.

rules.title: A Gig’s value cannot be adjusted to the value it already has.
rules.text:
6.4.5. A Gig’s value cannot be adjusted to the value it already has. If an effect tells you to do so, the effect fails.

rules.title: A value-pair is 2 dice with the same value in the same Gig area.
rules.text: 6.5. A value-pair is 2 dice with the same value in the same Gig area.

rules.title: A Gig can only count towards a single value-pair at a time.
rules.text:
6.5.1. A Gig can only count towards a single value-pair at a time.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit’s card text reads “Draw 1 for each friendly value-pair of Gigs.” And your Gig area contains three Gig dice with the same value: a d4, d6, and d8. The d4 and d6 may be counted as a value-pair, and then there are no more Gigs to pair with the d8. So, there is exactly one friendly value-pair of Gigs. Draw 1 card.

6.7.4. If a card effect triggers when a Gig would be stolen, resolve the effect after the Gig is selected, but before the Gig changes control.

> **EXAMPLE:** A Unit’s card text reads “When a rival Unit would steal a Gig, you may discard 1 with cost equal to that Gig's value. If you do, the Gig isn't stolen.” A rival Unit attacks your Gig area to steal 2 Gigs. Your Rival chooses to steal Gigs with values 3 and 10. You discard a card with cost 3, so the rival Unit only steals the value 10 Gig.

rules.text: 6.7.5. A Gig’s value can’t change during stealing. If an effect adjusts the Gig’s value, you must resolve it either before choosing the Gig(s), or after the Gig(s) change control.

rules.title: An effect is card text that affects the game.

rules.title: If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect.
rules.text: 10.1.4. If you control the source of an effect, it is considered “your” effect. You are the one who resolves it.

rules.title: After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.
rules.text: 10.2.5. After an effect resolves, perform any required rule processing before resolving a new one or taking any actions.

rules.title: An effect may include conditions.
rules.text: 10.3. An effect may include conditions. A “condition” is a requirement that must be true for an effect to apply, become pending, and resolve. (Conditions are often “if” or “when” clauses.)

rules.title: If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.
rules.text: 10.3.1. If a condition is false, do not apply its corresponding effect.

rules.text: 10.3.2. A condition is not a cost unless it is specifically within a cost. See Cost.

rules.title: A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.
rules.text: 10.3.3. A condition within an effect’s resolution is checked when that part of the effect resolves.

rules.text: 10.6. An effect is “invalid” if it cannot apply according to its text, the game rules, or the current game state.

rules.text: 10.6.2. If part of an effect is invalid, ignore the invalid part and resolve as much of the remaining effect as possible.

rules.text: 10.6.3. Even if an effect is invalid, it is still considered an effect on the card.

rules.text: 10.10. If an effect becomes invalid after it activates or becomes pending, still resolve as much of the effect as possible.

rules.title: A “pending” effect is an effect that is waiting to resolve.

rules.title: If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too.
rules.text: 10.14. If a new effect triggers while resolving one, the new effect enters pending too. Finish resolving the current pending effect before resolving any new pending effects.

rules.title: If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending eff…
rules.text: 10.14.1. If both players have a new effect enter pending while resolving an effect, the player currently resolving pending effects finishes resolving all of their pending effects (including the new ones) before their Rival resolves their new ones.

rules.title: Once an effect is pending, later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving (unless the effect…
rules.text: 10.15. Once an effect is pending, later changes to the game state do not stop that effect from resolving (unless the effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution).

rules.text: 10.15.1. If a pending effect includes a condition that must be true during resolution, that condition must still be true when the effect resolves.

rules.title: Activate an activated effect by completing these steps in order.

faqs.question: If a Unit or Legend with [DEFEATED] would be defeated but is prevented by an effect. Will I still get the [DEFEATED] effect?
If this Gear is attached to a Unit named "V" and the Unit attacks but is defeated before the end of the turn, can I still ready 2 Eddies?
Can I still play this card if I don't have more Street Cred than my Rival?
Do I have to defeat a rival Unit with power 5 or less, even if I don't want to?
Can I use this to defeat a Unit with 0 power if I do not have a friendly D20?
Can I defeat my own Unit with this effect?
If I do not control a friendly d20, can I play Over the Edge?
faqs.answer: Yes, but you cannot defeat a Unit.

faqs.question: When a Unit or Legend equipped with The Relic is defeated, do I move any equipped Gear on it to the bottom-deck, too?
faqs.answer: No. The Unit/Legend moves to the trash first, so any Gear (including The Relic) remains in the trash when you bottom-deck the Unit/Legend.

decisions.minotaur: Mandatory rival-only effective Unit defeat at current reference power<=5, conditional on current Street Cred>rival at resolution. False condition/no target does not invalidate Unit play.
decisions.overTheEdge: ANY effective Unit, including own; reference power<=at least one currently controlled rolled D20 value. No D20 selection is instructed; existential eligibility is equivalent to comparing with the maximum. No controlled D20 gives no targets, even power0; play still legal.
decisions.power: 3.17 and2.10.1: use shared current effective power (Gear/aura/temporary modifiers); negative retained as a characteristic but referenced as0. Null is not coerced; no admitted Null-power field Unit exists.
decisions.defeat: 9.19.1.1,4.12,5.9.4.1,11.19.2: shared semantic defeat declaration, owner Trash order, Gear follows/detaches, field Legend moves to REMOVED; capture DEFEATED bindings while active, enqueue after movement.
decisions.timing: 10.2.3/.4,10.14 and4.14: newly triggered effects enter pending after victim movement; finish current source effect, then immediately Trash resolving Program, before resolving DEFEATED effects. No interleaving or LIFO stack.
decisions.limits: Current two-player scopes and existing cross-owner card/Gear movement restriction remain. Read-only attack-aura queries do not grant Quick to either card.
